summary: This experimental IMAP extension lets servers announce a limit on the number of messages that one command can process, such as FETCH, SEARCH, STORE, COPY or MOVE. It helps servers control resource use.

eli5.summary: A mail server can say, ask for at most this many messages at a time, so no one request is too large.

questions: how to limit messages per imap command
what does the imap messagelimit response code mean
what are imap uidafter and uidbefore
subtitle: A way for an IMAP server to announce how many messages one command may touch, so clients can work in batches.

tldr.problem: Huge mailboxes let a single IMAP command such as FETCH or SEARCH touch an enormous number of messages, which costs the server a lot of memory and work.
tldr.mechanism: The server advertises a MESSAGELIMIT=N capability (N is a positive integer). When a command would exceed it, the server processes messages from highest to lowest UID and returns a MESSAGELIMIT response code naming the lowest UID it handled, so the client can repeat the command for the rest.
tldr.outcome: Servers can bound resource use and clients know the limit up front. Clients that do not understand the extension may see odd results in large mailboxes, so the RFC suggests phasing enforcement in.

today: RFC 9738 was published in March 2025 as an Experimental RFC. It has not been obsoleted or updated according to the metadata.

sections.title: Why a Message Limit
sections.content:
The MESSAGELIMIT extension lets an IMAP server announce a limit on the number of messages that can be processed in a single FETCH, SEARCH, STORE, COPY or MOVE command (or their UID variants), or in a single APPEND or UID EXPUNGE command.

This helps servers control resource usage. It also helps clients, which learn the limit and can avoid issuing commands that would exceed it. The extension works with both IMAP4rev1 (RFC 3501) and IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051). This RFC is Experimental, not a Standards Track document.
sections.eli5: If everyone asked the librarian for every book at once, she would be buried. This lets her say how many books she hands over per request.

sections.title: Advertising the Limit
sections.content:
A server advertises support by including MESSAGELIMIT=<limit> in its CAPABILITY response or response code, where the limit is a positive integer. The advertised limit SHOULD NOT be lower than 1000 messages.

A server that only enforces a limit on COPY and APPEND (and their UID variants) advertises SAVELIMIT=<limit> instead.
sections.eli5: The server puts up a sign: 'Maximum this many messages per request.' A server that only limits copying and saving puts up a different sign.

sections.title: The MESSAGELIMIT Response Code
sections.content:
If a server will not operate on more than N messages in one COPY or UID COPY, it MUST fail the command with a tagged NO carrying the MESSAGELIMIT response code, and no messages are copied, since copy has to be atomic.

For SEARCH, FETCH, STORE, MOVE, APPEND and UID EXPUNGE, the server MUST return the MESSAGELIMIT response code, which gives the limit and the lowest processed UID. When it is returned, the server is REQUIRED to process messages from highest to lowest UID. The client repeats the operation for the remaining messages, adjusting the message set for MOVE and STORE as needed, until the response code is no longer returned or a tagged NO or BAD arrives.

The server MUST NOT impose any limit on plain EXPUNGE, CLOSE or STATUS UNSEEN. When the PARTIAL extension is used and the requested range exceeds the limit, the example shows the server refusing to do any work and replying NO. When both EXPUNGEISSUED and MESSAGELIMIT must be returned, the former goes in the tagged OK and the latter in an untagged NO.
sections.eli5: If you ask for too many, the server hands you the newest batch and says, 'I stopped at this one.' You then ask for the older ones next.

sections.title: UIDAFTER, UIDBEFORE and Related Extensions
sections.content:
The extension adds two SEARCH keys. UIDAFTER <uid> matches messages with a UID greater than the given UID, the same as UID <uid>+1:*. UIDBEFORE <uid> matches messages with a smaller UID, the same as UID 1:<uid>-1, or the empty set if the UID is 1. They are especially useful with SEARCHRES and can be pipelined.

For THREAD, a server advertising MESSAGELIMIT N will be unable to run it in a mailbox with more than N messages. SORT might also be unavailable unless the server maintains indices for its sort orders. If the server supports SEARCHRES, it MUST truncate the saved $ result when a SEARCH succeeds but MESSAGELIMIT is returned. With MULTIAPPEND, the limit applies to APPEND and no messages are appended when it is exceeded.
sections.eli5: Two new search words let you say 'everything newer than this one' or 'everything older,' which makes asking for the next batch easy.

sections.title: Compatibility With Older Clients
sections.content:
Clients that do not know the extension are affected only in mailboxes with more than N messages. There, copying more than N messages always fails, and commands like FETCH, SEARCH and MOVE are effectively restricted to the last N messages. Unextended searches used to count messages would return incorrect counts. EXPUNGE and CLOSE are not affected.

The RFC gives an example of a mailing list with about 1500 posts a week and a limit of 1000: the returning user's client downloads only 1000 messages and acts as if the server is broken. To give clients time to adapt, servers can advertise a limit without enforcing it for a while, or advertise 1000 but enforce a higher, unadvertised hard limit such as 10,000. Attempts to exceed the limit can be logged to track client support.
sections.eli5: Old email programs do not know about the sign and may only see the newest batch, so the server can go easy on enforcing it at first.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The extension does not change the security considerations of IMAP4rev1 or IMAP4rev2. Because it reduces the work a server does and the data a client receives, it can lower memory use and help protect against denial-of-service attacks. It is new code on both sides, so the RFC calls for rigorous testing to avoid new bugs.

IANA added the MESSAGELIMIT= and SAVELIMIT= capabilities to the IMAP Capabilities registry.
sections.eli5: Smaller batches mean less strain on the server, but new code can have new mistakes, so test it well.
